newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - GAP CFO sees same store sales up.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - GAP CFO sees same store sales up.

text.p: Gap Inc chief financial officer Warren Hashagen said he expects modestly positive comparable store sales for the second half of 1996.
Earlier, Gap reported comparable store sales for August 1996 were flat versus a six percent drop in August 1995.
"Our expectations would be for modestly positive comparable store sales in the second half," Hashager said.
"My view of the month is that it is four weeks out of the quarter. It was less than expected but not predictive of the balance of the year," he said.
Hashagen said other fashion assortments did well and noted denim sales are a bigger factor in August than other months.

"The basic entry price-point denim business is a back to school business, so it should not be the same issue in the September," he said, adding, "August is a month when denim is promoted by our competition and its a one-month issue"
He said Gap's success in the rest of the third quarter and balance of the year will depend on fashion assortments.
Hashagen also cited good inventory control. "Inventories are very well-controlled. They are very low," he said.
